newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angry crowd attacks UNITA officials in Angolan town.
newsitem.headline: Angry crowd attacks UNITA officials in Angolan town.

text.p: Two senior officials of Angola's opposition UNITA movement were beaten by a crowd in a UNITA-held town being handed over to the unity government on Friday, Angolan state radio reported.

The radio said UNITA's representative on the Joint Commission with the government, Isaias Samakuva, and the Vice Minister of Territorial Administration Miguel N'zau Puna, were stoned by a crowd of about 300 UNITA supporters.
The men were attending a ceremony in the town of Quibala in Kwaza Zul province to formally turn over the area to government control.
"People have to be educated about this process," Samakuva told the radio. "If they are not properly informed we are bound to see more of these nasty incidents."
Both men were evacuated and treated in a Luanda military hospital. An army captain at the hospital told Reuters the men suffered minor injuries to the face and had been released.

The Angolan peace process began in 1994 when the government and UNITA signed a pact to end two decades of civil war. Although the factions became partners in a unity government in April, the former rebels still control vast areas of the country.
